summary.en: These words join two ideas that seem opposite. **Although, though, even though** + clause; **in spite of / despite** + noun or -ing; **however** starts a new sentence; **whereas / while** compares two facts. Pick the pattern that fits the grammar: _Although it rained, we went out_; _Despite the rain, we went out_; _It rained. However, we went out._
summary.es: «Aunque» se dice although + oración; «a pesar de» se dice despite/in spite of + nombre o -ing. Nunca despite of ni in spite that.

form: **Although / though / even though** + subject + verb (_Although she was tired, …_)
**In spite of / despite** + noun or -ing (_despite the delay_, _in spite of feeling ill_); **despite the fact that** + clause
**However** + comma, in a new sentence (_However, we decided to stay._); **but** joins two clauses without commas
**Whereas / while** + clause to contrast two things (_He likes tea, whereas I prefer coffee._)
**Even though** is stronger than although; **though** can come at the end in speech (_It's nice. Expensive, though._)

uses.text: **Surprising result**: _**Although** he trained hard, he lost the race._
**Noun or -ing after despite**: _**Despite** the traffic, we arrived early._ _**In spite of** being tired, she stayed up._

note.en: Despite is never followed by of. In spite takes of.
note.es: Despite no lleva of; in spite sí: in spite of.

uses.text: **Starting a new sentence**: _The offer was generous. **However**, she turned it down._
**Comparing two things**: _Spain is hot in summer, **whereas** Scotland is cool._
**Stronger emphasis**: _**Even though** I had studied, I felt nervous._

mistakes.wrong: Despite of the rain, we had a picnic.
mistakes.right: Despite the rain, we had a picnic.

why.en: Despite is not followed by of; in spite of is.

mistakes.wrong: Although the rain, we went out.
mistakes.right: Although it was raining, we went out.

why.en: Although needs a full clause. Use despite with a noun.
why.es: Although lleva oración completa; con un nombre, despite.

mistakes.wrong: Although he was tired, but he kept working.
mistakes.right: Although he was tired, he kept working.

why.en: Do not use but together with although.
why.es: No uses although y but a la vez, como en «aunque… pero».

mistakes.wrong: It was cheap, however it was poor quality.
mistakes.right: It was cheap. However, it was poor quality.

why.en: However needs a full stop or semicolon before it and a comma after it.
why.es: However no une dos oraciones con una coma; empieza una nueva.

examples.en: Although the film was long, I enjoyed every minute.
examples.es: Aunque la película era larga, disfruté cada minuto.

examples.en: In spite of the high price, the flat sold quickly.
examples.es: A pesar del precio alto, el piso se vendió rápido.

examples.en: Despite feeling ill, she gave an excellent presentation.
Even though I'd slept for ten hours, I was exhausted.
The first option is cheaper. However, the second is more reliable.
My brother loves cities, whereas I prefer the countryside.
Despite the fact that he had little experience, he got the job.
It's a good restaurant. Rather noisy, though.
While some people enjoy remote work, others find it lonely.

practice.prompt: ___ the heavy traffic, we reached the airport on time.

explanation.en: Despite is followed by a noun phrase: the heavy traffic.

practice.prompt: She enjoyed the course ___ it was very demanding.

explanation.en: A full clause follows, so we need even though.

practice.prompt: The hotel was clean. ___, the staff were rude.

explanation.en: However begins a new sentence to show contrast.

practice.prompt: Tom prefers trains, ___ Anna always flies.
